newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Ekeus leaves for Saudi after Kuwait visit.
newsitem.headline: Ekeus leaves for Saudi after Kuwait visit.

text.p: The United Nations official in charge of eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction left for Saudi Arabia on Sunday as part of a Gulf tour aimed at securing funds for his commission, diplomats said.
Rolf Ekeus left Kuwait after a three-day visit during which he discussed the commission's efforts to end Baghdad's missile, biological and chemical arms capabilities.
Ekeus last year went on a similar Gulf Arab tour ahead of an annual Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit to ask for $90 million over three years to finance his commission.
Diplomats said Ekeus has reiterated the need for financial contributions for his five-year-old commission by Gulf Arab states who will hold their 1996 summit in Qatar in December.
The last summit said Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain would extend political and financial support but did not specify an amount.

Qatar later blasted the U.N. for treating oil-rich GCC states as bankrollers for its global operations, saying that GCC members had agreed to provide the commission with funds but proportional to the six states' general U.N. quotas.
GCC states fought alongside the United States-led 1991 Gulf War coalition that liberated Kuwait from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
